title.narrative: Plastic Waste Management: Towards a New Social Contract in Partnership with the Private sector

description.narrative: The Republic of Djibouti faces major challenges in the collection, management, and treatment of waste—especially plastic waste—in both urban and rural areas. Municipalities are currently responsible for waste management, but they face significant obstacles: approximately 344 tons of waste are generated daily, of which 20% is plastic—a volume that continues to rise due to population growth and urbanization. This situation is further hampered by the lack of official, reliable, and accessible data, as well as limited coordination, which prevents the implementation of effective solutions. Additionally, Djiboutis private sector, still in its early stages of development, suffers from structural constraints, notably limited access to diversified financing mechanisms. Young entrepreneurs, micro-businesses, and SMEs struggle to mobilize the resources needed to develop innovative projects, particularly in waste management. The weakness of the private sector thus hinders the emergence of new and dynamic solutions, which are essential for a successful green transition.
